subject: Solarwind: surge-window uptime/latency exception request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Solarwind follow-up + attachments (surge window ask)

Team — quick note after the call with Solarwind earlier. Lena and Tom laid out a narrow but critical request: during their nightly indexing surge (PST 18:00–20:00), they want an elevated p95 latency commitment (target ~40–50ms) for a subset of requests that power their nearline search. The rest of the day they are happy with our standard p95. They also asked for an explicit throughput reservation for that 2-hour window to avoid degraded tails.

I attached a draft SLA and an operational runbook they asked to see (SLA-draft-v2.pdf, operational-runbook.docx). Key asks for internal review:
- Confirm tech feasibility for a temporary, scheduled carveout (2 hours nightly) that reduces p95 to ~50ms for the identified route.
- High-level cost delta/GPU footprint for the carveout.
- Any required product changes or routing controls (can we do this with current routing + dedicated burst pool?).
- A short runbook for fallback (what we do if we miss the p95 during the surge).

They signalled urgency — Solarwind is in final procurement but conditioned on having this defined. Deal is SW-2027-0143 (strategic account). Please review and reply with what you need (metrics, QPS, sample traces). If we can, I want to get a technical + commercial answer back to them by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Naomi
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solarwind follow-up + attachments (surge window ask)

Naomi — thanks for the summary. Short take: technically doable but with tradeoffs.

What we can offer with the current platform:
- Scheduled dedicated burst pool: spin up a small dedicated pool (node group) that is only in the routing topology during 18:00–20:00 PST. That isolates latency for the carveout but increases cost because capacity sits idle outside the window.
- Smart routing + prefix KV cache tagging: if Solarwind can scope the request patterns (which endpoints / prompt shapes), we can pre-warm KV cache and reduce cold tails.
- Fallback: automatic routing to a lower-cost variant with a clearly documented latency delta. We should add a circuit-breaker to avoid L7 queueing.

Required inputs from Sales/Customer:
- Expected concurrent QPS during the 2-hour window and distribution across routes (numbers please).
- Typical sequence length / tokens distribution for the indexed flow.
- Any hard SLA penalty thresholds we need to honor.

Rough cost order-of-magnitude: dedicated burst pool sized to sustain their stated QPS would be roughly $10k–$15k/month if we reserve the nodes and amortize setup. If we use ephemeral preemptible-style capacity just for the window, operational complexity / failure rate goes up (higher risk).

I can draft a short operational runbook update once we have QPS and token estimates. If they want a 3-month pilot, we can propose a pilot pricing and a sunset clause.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena@solarwind.ai>, Tom Becker <t.becker@solarwind.ai>
Date: 2025-07-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solarwind follow-up + attachments (surge window ask)

Adding customer context — Lena / Tom, thanks for staying on this. Per our commercial posture: Solarwind is targeting a Q3 go-live for search improvements tied to this commit. They indicated they can sign a 12-month commitment if we provide a clear short-term carveout and a firm pilot plan. They also attached redlines to the SLA (solarwind-redlines.xlsx).

From the customer call: typical concurrent QPS during the surge is 380–540 rps, bursts up to ~900rps for 5–10 minutes. Average sequence length is ~220 tokens; about 25% of calls hit the heavy retrieval path. They need the low-p95 promise only for the retrieval endpoint (not all traffic).

Action items for us:
- Karthik: confirm sizing for a 600rps steady target with 900rps burst headroom for 10 mins.
- Sean: list the operational controls we need to expose to Solarwind (monitoring dashboards, alert thresholds, on-call escalation).
- Connor: this will need a carveout clause in the contract; can you prep a short exception template legal can insert?

We need to move quickly — customer is pushing procurement team to get final terms by next week.

Marissa
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solarwind follow-up + attachments (surge window ask)

Quick operational notes:
- Runbook changes: we'll add a `scheduled-surge` path that pre-warms caches, pins routing to the dedicated pool, and raises an on-call P1 if p95 breaches the threshold for >3 consecutive minutes.
- Monitoring: create a per-route dashboard (p50/p95/p99, QPS, concurrency, CPU/GPU utilization) and grant read access to Solarwind's SRE account for the pilot.
- Fallback behavior: if dedicated pool underperforms, route to fallback model with explicit latency expectation and run emergency throttling to protect platform stability.

Operational gating questions for Product/Infra:
1) Can product enable an API flag to mark requests as "surge-scoped" so routing is safe and customers can't mislabel traffic? (This avoids customers gaming the carveout.)
2) Is a nightly scheduled spin-up automated today or do we need a small infra change to orchestrate the pool creation + warmup?

Related items: HubSpot link to deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890) and proposed DocuSign route for SLA (https://www.docusign.net/signature/ABCDEF-123456). I recommend we hold contractual language minimal and rely on pilot metrics for longer-term commitments.

Sean
Head of Customer Operations
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-05T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solarwind follow-up + attachments (surge window ask)

Thanks everyone — looping back with a proposed path so we can give Solarwind a single-threaded answer by EOD Friday.

Proposed decision (needs confirmation from Product/legal/commercial):
- Offer a 3-month pilot with a nightly 18:00–20:00 PST dedicated burst pool sized for 600rps steady with 900rps short bursts.
- Pilot pricing: one-time setup + $12k/month for the dedicated capacity (approx. estimate from Karthik).
- Provide Solarwind SRE read-only dashboards for the pilot and a signed carveout clause that expires at pilot end unless both sides agree to extend.
- Tech controls: require a customer-side request flag `surge_scope=true` for routing; internal validation in infra to prevent abuse.

Connor — can you draft the carveout language and a short signature-ready amendment? Karthik/Sean — if you can confirm the 600rps/900rps sizing and any infra changes required by EOD, Naomi will send the customer the pilot proposal.

(Attached: SLA-draft-v2.pdf, operational-runbook.docx)
